text.p: LONDON Sept 12 (Reuter) Anglo-Australian mining giant RTZ-CRA Thursday reported a 22 percent plunge in earnings for the first half of the year, blaming the fall mainly on lower metal prices.
But the firm was upbeat that metal demand and prices would improve during the rest of this year and into 1997.
The company said its income slumped to $552 million from $711 million a year earlier.
Metal prices cut earnings by $194 million due to crumbling copper prices and exchange rate fluctuations lowered profits by $34 million, it said.
Copper prices averaged $1.15 a pound in the first half of 1996, down 13 percent from a year ago and prices have since slumped to less than 90 cents so far in the second half.
Every 10-cent fall in the price of copper hits net earnings by $90 million, according to RTZ-CRA's own estimates.
RTZ-CRA said that it was optimistic that metal demand would improve.

"On a longer-term view, we are confident about growth of demand, especially from the Asian region which now accounts for a significant share of global consumption of all metals and minerals," said Chairman Sir Derek Birkin.
